title: ADR: quality-aware priority scheduling for fidelity tiering
author: Lena Park
body:
Summary:

This ADR records the decision to implement a quality-aware priority scheduling layer in the inference routing stack that factors model output quality (measured against per-customer prompt sets and golden responses), client fidelity tier, and cost/latency signals when placing requests into execution queues or selecting fallback model variants. The goal is to transparently maintain application-level quality SLOs while optimizing GPU utilization and keeping latency within tiered SLAs.

Status:
- Decision: Accept the quality-aware priority scheduler (QAPS) design described below.
- Scope: Redwood API routing + Dedicated routing + Private runtime-side scheduler.

Context and motivation:
- We operate multi-variant serving (high-fidelity, medium-fidelity, quantized/low-cost variants) and provide tiered client fidelity (premium/standard/economy).
- Current routing uses static priority + cost hints which can cause blind quality regressions when capacity is constrained (canary incidents where low-cost fallbacks increased semantic errors).
- We need a runtime mechanism that: 1) preserves quality for high-value traffic; 2) minimizes overall cost when quality budget allows; 3) provides clear observability and safety gates for rollouts.

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals:
  - Maintain per-route quality SLOs (see "Observability and SLOs").
  - Make scheduling decisions using a compact score composed of: fidelity_weight, recent_quality_delta, client_priority, latency_headroom, and cost_penalty.
  - Provide a soft admission control to redirect or queue requests when risk of quality regression is high.
- Non-goals:
  - Do not change model training, on-line learning, or evaluation tooling.
  - QAPS will not attempt to alter prompts or perform automated prompt engineering. That remains at product layer.

Decision details (design):
1) Score composition
   - Each incoming request is annotated with: requested_fidelity (premium/standard/economy), route_id, client_tier, prompt_hash, and an optional quality_hint (from the client).
   - Scheduler computes Quality Score (QS) where higher QS means higher scheduling precedence: 
     QS = Wf * FidelityBias + Wq * RecentQualityDelta(route_id,prompt_hash) + Wc * ClientPriority - Wcost * CostPenalty(device,variant) - Wlat * LatencyRisk
   - Default weights: Wf=3, Wq=5, Wc=2, Wcost=1, Wlat=1. Weights are configurable per-cluster via config service.

2) RecentQualityDelta
   - A rolling window aggregate (exponential moving average) of per-route prompt-set quality delta vs baseline (measured by offline/eval and production A/B probes). Range: [-10, +10], unitless percent points.
   - Positive values favor scheduling (indicates improvement), negative values reduce priority.

3) Admission and fallback rules
   - If QS >= threshold_high => schedule to preferred high-fidelity pool.
   - If threshold_low <= QS < threshold_high => schedule to medium-fidelity pool or queue with short wait (see queuing policy).
   - If QS < threshold_low => consider routing to low-cost variant only if client_tier == economy OR if client explicitly allows degraded mode.
   - Thresholds (default): threshold_high=6, threshold_low=1. Configurable per-tenant.

4) Short-window queued probing
   - When the high-fidelity pool is saturated but QS indicates potential quality risk, place requests in a short head-aware pending queue (max 50ms) and soft-probe a small number (2%) of warm fast-path instances to validate quality under load before deciding fallback.

5) Safety gates and rollback
   - Any change to weights or thresholds must pass a gated rollout: 0% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% traffic with synthetic quality probes and automatic rollback on defined health signals.

Operational details:
- Services and components involved:
  - router (edge) — annotates requests and forwards to scheduler API. Owner: edge-team.
  - qaps-scheduler (new service) — computes QS, consults quality telemetry cache, returns route decision. Owner: runtime-team.
  - fleet-orchestrator — applies decision to model variant selection and queue placement. Owner: infra-team.
  - quality-probe-agent — background probe executor that runs golden prompt checks and updates RecentQualityDelta. Owner: applied-ml.

- Data flows:
  1) router -> qaps-scheduler (request metadata)
  2) qaps-scheduler -> telemetry-store (fetch RecentQualityDelta, client_tier)
  3) qaps-scheduler -> fleet-orchestrator (decision)
  4) fleet-orchestrator -> runtime (dispatch)

Rollout and migration plan (high level):
1) Implement scheduler in shadow mode (decisions logged, not enforced) for 2 weeks across 10% of traffic.
2) Add synthetic quality probes for top 50 routes; verify RecentQualityDelta accuracy.
3) Enable soft-serving (queueing only) at 5% traffic with manual guardrails.
4) Run staged rollout to 25% then 100% with automated gating thresholds.

Observability and SLOs:
- Quality SLOs (per-route):
  - Golden-set accuracy: p95 >= 96% for premium routes; p95 >= 92% for standard routes; economy has no quality SLO but must not regress more than 5 percentage points vs baseline without explicit consent.
  - Allowed production quality delta: premium <= +/−1.5pp, standard <= +/−3pp over a 24h window.
- Latency SLOs (unchanged):
  - Premium: p95 < 80ms; p99 < 250ms.
  - Standard: p95 < 200ms; p99 < 500ms.
- Monitoring and alerts:
  - Alert: production_quality_delta(route_id) > configured_delta for 10 minutes -> SEV-2, page runtime oncall.
  - Alert: scheduler_decision_error_rate > 0.5% -> SEV-3, page infra oncall.
  - Dashboards: per-tenant quality heatmap, QS distribution histogram, queued-probe success rate.

Compatibility and API changes:
- Router-to-scheduler API
  - POST /scheduler/score (JSON)
    - payload fields: request_id, route_id, prompt_hash, requested_fidelity, client_tier, quality_hint (optional), timeout_ms
    - response: { decision: "high|medium|low|queue", reason_code, expected_latency_ms }
- Backwards compatibility
  - If qaps-scheduler is unavailable, router falls back to current static-priority logic and emits a telemetry tag 'qaps_down'.

Security and privacy considerations:
- RecentQualityDelta uses hashed prompt identifiers; raw prompts are not sent to scheduler. Only small sampled probes include raw prompts and are protected by access controls.
- Telemetry retention for QS metadata follows PII minimization policy: prompt-level hashes retained 30 days, aggregates retained 13 months.

Operational runbook (short):
1) If golden-set accuracy alert fires for a premium route:
   a) Check qaps-scheduler recent quality delta and probe success rate.
   b) If QAPS indicates negative delta, temporarily increase Wcost and set threshold_high to +inf (force high-fidelity placement) for affected route and escalate to applied-ml.
   c) If no QAPS signal, check model variant health and fallback-orchestrator logs for preemption/eviction events.
2) If scheduler_decision_error_rate elevated:
   a) Check telemetry-store connectivity and cache TTLs.
   b) Flip router to fallback static-priority (feature flag), notify infra team, and roll qaps-scheduler to previous stable config.

Consequences and trade-offs:
- Pros:
  - Reduces silent quality regressions by explicitly incorporating quality signals into scheduling.
  - Provides granular per-route/tenant controls and clear rollback semantics.
- Cons:
  - Introduces added runtime complexity and an additional operational surface (qaps-scheduler + probes).
  - Risk of noisy signals from sparse probes causing oscillation; mitigated via EMA smoothing and rollout gates.

Open questions and future work:
- Investigate machine-learned QS models (replace linear weight sum) after 6 months of telemetry.
- Tie QAPS decisions to cost accounting to surface per-request expected spend to billing pipelines.

References and related docs:
- See runtime-workload-signatures-and-slo-derivation-playbook-2024 for SLO composition rules.
- See continuous-fallback-orchestration-for-multi-variant-serving-standards-2026 for variant compatibility matrices.
